title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
statement:
Given a binary search tree (BST), find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) node of two given nodes with values `p` and `q` in the BST.

The lowest common ancestor is defined as the lowest node in the tree that has both `p` and `q` as descendants (where a node can be a descendant of itself).

Build a real `TreeNode` BST from `values`, then use the BST ordering property to navigate directly toward the split point instead of a general tree search.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 10^5]
p and q will exist in the BST

editorial.approach: Starting at the root, compare both `p` and `q` to the current node's value. If both are smaller, the LCA must be in the left subtree, so move left. If both are larger, move right. As soon as `p` and `q` fall on different sides (or one equals the current node's value), the current node is the split point and therefore the LCA.
editorial.complexity: O(h) time / O(1) space (iterative), where h is the tree height
